title: Arrest of the whole band in Memphis over a bus and Mrs. Collins
summary: Police arrested the band after a dispute over the chartered bus and Johnny Collins's wife, an officer asked why they had not shot Armstrong in the leg, and bags took ten men to unload.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I've read where Johnny Collins the manager's wife travelled with the band on that tour.
Yeah, that's right.
And that you got into Memphis, and some cops arrested the whole band because she was on the bus.

That's right. They certainly did. They arrested the whole band. And they came in and at the time, she was sitting in the seat, and Louis -- she was telling Louis something, Louis was on the edge of the arm of the bus, that's what it was, the arm of the seat, when the guys came in. And told the other -- (inaudible). When you stop to think of some of these things, you know, they are quite -- because some of the things that people that are sick-minded, you know, and still be ignorant. It's pain, but it's comical.
Told him, says -- told the captain, says, "You know what?" Oh, I forgot this recording, I forgot. He said, "He said this big, burly blankety-blankety-blank was sitting on
the arm of the seat that this white woman was sitting. So this guy said, "Why didn't you shoot him in the leg?"
Oh, really?
Isn't that something? Sure. That's what he said. "Why didn't you shoot him in the leg?"
God. That's unbelievable.

So -- yeah, so the only one that didn't get thrown in the clanker was Mike McKendrick. He was out somewhere, doing something and he didn't get a chance to get into that. And the whole thing was, the bus that Mrs. Collins had chartered was to take us from Jackson to Little Rock.

Well, they carried us from Jackson to Memphis, and then they wanted to change the bus. They wanted us to get into a different bus. Well, she said, "No, I want -- the bus that I want them to have --" so Louis could have this seat, to ra'r back in, to sleep. But they wanted to give us a little bus with the seats sitting straight up this way.
And that was the whole thing.
I see.
Yeah, they didn't want to do it, so this bus driver called the cops, and the cops said, Take them to the station.
Oh, the bus driver was the one that did it.
Yeah, so he said, "You know, every

trusty -- we had to have every trusty that he have in the clanker to come out, they had so much baggage, to get that baggage out." Because I had my piano accordion, I had the piano accordion, my Gladstone, my trumpet case, and then also my ordinary suitcase, see. And the carryall bag. See, we had carryall bags that we had shaving mugs and things in it.
Yeah.
And everybody had at least four or five -- you it'd take ten men --
That's a lot of baggage.
Was a lot of baggage.
Well, how did you get out?
The manager of the theatre where we had to come back to from Little Rock, we had to come back there and play after we played our engagement in Little Rock --
back to Memphis.
Memphis, he got them out. And then we caught the train, we had to catch a train, and we were late getting to Little Rock, but the crowd was still there. We got to Little Rock about 12:00.
Midnight?
Midnight, and they were still there, waiting on us.
